all-drive-no-drop-pickleball.name: All Drive No Drop Pickleball
all-drive-no-drop-pickleball.bio: The channel behind the All Drive No Drop Pickleball Podcast, hosted with David from Tickle My Pickleball. Its paddle reviews often list swing weight, twist weight and spin RPM, and cover many elongated Gen 3 and Gen 4 paddles.

amirs-pickleball.name: Amir's Pickleball
amirs-pickleball.bio: A channel with pickleball tips, gear reviews and gameplay. Its paddle reviews often add 3 g weight pods and compare paddles to ones they played before, such as Luzz Inferno and Six Zero Black Opal.

axel-lee-pickleball.name: Axel Lee Pickleball
axel-lee-pickleball.bio: A paddle reviewer in Malaysia. Reviews are built on 20 to 30 hours of play per paddle, with measured static, swing and twist weights, and attention to how grit changes over time.

bepickleballer.name: bepickleballer
bepickleballer.bio: A blog and TikTok creator who writes ranked paddle comparisons. Reviews place paddles in lists for 2026 and budget picks, and compare close siblings such as the Enhance EPP and MPP Turbo.

bp2-pickleball.name: BP2 Pickleball
bp2-pickleball.bio: A channel covering pickleball in Asia. Reviews describe several days to weeks of dinking, counters and live games, and often mention grit durability and how foam and Gen 3 paddles differ.

briones-pickleball-academy.name: Briones Pickleball Academy
briones-pickleball-academy.bio: A channel from Jordan Briones, who writes of a decade of experience and helping players improve. Paddle reviews often add lead tape and compare paddles side by side, including several Six Zero and Selkirk models.

briones-pickleball-breakdown.name: Briones Pickleball Breakdown
briones-pickleball-breakdown.bio: A channel that turns real matches into lessons. Its paddle reviews report swing weight and twist weight, often mention lead tape, and point out who each paddle suits, from beginners to intermediate players.

cody-childers.name: Cody Childers
cody-childers.bio: The creator behind Dink N Donuts, a channel of reviews, tips and humorous videos. Reviews give clear breakdowns of power, spin and feel, sometimes scored out of 10, and often cover elongated and hybrid paddles.

daniel-pickleball.name: Daniel Pickleball
daniel-pickleball.bio: A paddle review channel. Reviews score power, control, spin and sweet spot out of 10, and cover widebodies and Gen 3 style paddles from brands such as Neonic and Paddletek.

ddog-pickleball.name: DDOG_Pickleball
ddog-pickleball.bio: A channel with reviews, updates and entertainment from across the pickleball world. Its paddle reviews often describe tungsten tape setups and compare new foam paddles with earlier Gen 3 ones, including first impressions of units sent by brands.

derik-hyndman-pickleball.name: Derik Hyndman Pickleball
derik-hyndman-pickleball.bio: A collegiate pickleball player who reviews paddles. Reviews often rank paddles within a line, such as the Joola Pro V group, and warn about core crush and delamination reports.

dink-kage-pickleball.name: Dink Kagè Pickleball
dink-kage-pickleball.bio: A channel with pickleball tips, tricks and daily vlogs. Its paddle reviews focus on Joola paddles, comparing Perseus, Agassi and Hyperion models from on-court play after moving over from earlier versions.

dinking-and-driving.name: Dinking And Driving
dinking-and-driving.bio: A paddle review channel that covers Luzz, Six Zero and Selkirk models, plus Gen 4 foam paddles. Reviews often compare new releases with earlier versions and note when a unit was a preview or a free sample.

drill-more-pickleball.name: Drill More Pickleball
drill-more-pickleball.bio: A YouTube and TikTok channel focused on pickleball, with links and discounts listed in its description. Its paddle reviews often cover widebody and hybrid shapes and say how added weight changes the sweet spot.

dwell-time-pickleball.name: Dwell Time Pickleball
dwell-time-pickleball.bio: A channel offering paddle reviews and on-court testing aimed at helping players find gear that fits their game. Reviews give static, swing and twist weights and focus on dwell, grit durability and power tier.

dy-pickleball.name: DY Pickleball
dy-pickleball.bio: A channel and Substack covering game highlights, instruction and paddle reviews. Their reviews compare new paddles with ones they have played for dozens of games, often Honolulu models, and comment on grit and break-in.

famous-by-friday-pickleball.name: Famous by Friday Pickleball
famous-by-friday-pickleball.bio: A channel that tests paddles over a few weeks with warm-ups, cone drills and serve speed checks. Reviews list static weight, swing weight and twist weight, and compare serve speed against a normal 50 mph.

farmer-lanky-pickleball.name: Farmer Lanky Pickleball
farmer-lanky-pickleball.bio: A channel for paddle reviews, comparisons and testing. Reviews record spin in RPM, swing weight and twist weight, rate power and pop by tier, and say which player ratings can handle each paddle.

francis-rances-pickleball.name: Francis Rances Pickleball
francis-rances-pickleball.bio: A Filipino amateur player based in the US, sponsored by Team Gearbox Pickleball according to the channel. Their paddle reviews focus on 11SIX24 and Joola models, with notes on added weight, swing weight and break-in.

infotechyeti.name: InfoTechYeti
infotechyeti.bio: A channel run by a CompTIA Network+ certified computer technician who shares simple gear reviews. Their paddle reviews often compare two or three paddles directly, including against the Bread & Butter Loco and Honolulu J2FC+.

jj-pickleball.name: JJ Pickleball
jj-pickleball.bio: A channel that reviews paddles, pickleballs and bags. Their paddle reviews report swing weight, twist weight and spin tests in RPM, and often comment on how well the grit holds up.

john-wilkerson-pickleball.name: John Wilkerson - Pickleball
john-wilkerson-pickleball.bio: A channel by a player whose stated main paddle is the Vatic Pro V-Sol Tour 16mm Flash. Their reviews describe shots from the baseline to the kitchen and say which skill levels each paddle suits, often intermediate to advanced.

johnkew-pickleball.name: Johnkew Pickleball
johnkew-pickleball.bio: A channel whose stated goal is to show how data changes what players should believe about paddles. Reviews combine lab measurements such as human-generated spin, firepower and spin durability with on-court play.

jordan-plays-pickle-jordan-irwin.name: Jordan Plays Pickle (Jordan Irwin)
jordan-plays-pickle-jordan-irwin.bio: Jordan Plays Pickle is a YouTube channel that reviews and discusses pickleball. Their paddle reviews cover power, pop, spin, control, sweet spot and twist weight, often compared against other paddles they have played, including Vatic Pro, Joola and Bread & Butter models.

kev-knows-pickleball.name: Kev Knows Pickleball
kev-knows-pickleball.bio: A channel describing itself as a one stop shop for all things pickleball. Reviews often report measured static, swing and twist weights after roughly 8 to 30 hours of play, including several CRBN paddles.

limitless-pickleball.name: Limitless Pickleball
limitless-pickleball.bio: A channel by a PPR certified pickleball instructor who says they have taught over 1000 students. Reviews often compare paddles within the RPM and Six Zero lines, including grit wear checks after months of play.

maiko.name: Maiko
maiko.bio: A channel by a player who describes themselves as just a pickler who loves trying new paddles. Reviews report swing weight, twist weight and balance point, mostly for power paddles bought with their own money.

martin-grunin-pickleball.name: Martin Grunin Pickleball
martin-grunin-pickleball.bio: A channel by a former competitive D1 tennis player who recently took up pickleball. Reviews describe many hours of play with RPM and Joola paddles, and sometimes note how added weight changes the feel.

matthew-k-pickleball.name: Matthew K Pickleball 🏓
matthew-k-pickleball.bio: A pickleball gear reviewer, YouTuber and podcaster. Reviews cover many foam paddles, with frequent comments on grit and durability, and sometimes add a few grams of tungsten weight.

matts-pickleball.name: Matt's Pickleball
matts-pickleball.bio: A channel that says its paddle reviews are built on measured data, using the same instruments on every paddle. Reviews report swing weight, twist weight, serve speed, spin in RPM and grit roughness, sometimes after 30 or more hours of play.

mid-century-pickleball.name: Mid-Century Pickleball
mid-century-pickleball.bio: A Milwaukee based channel covering pickleball. Reviews are often two-host discussions after several hours of play, with demos for other players, and compare paddles within the Joola, Gearbox and Six Zero lines.

mypicklelist.name: MyPickleList
mypicklelist.bio: A paddle review blog that publishes first-impressions reviews after a few days of play, often on units sent by brands or borrowed. Reviews cover pop, sweet spot, feel and resets, and some add weight at 3 and 9 o'clock.

mypicklelist-pickle-li.name: MyPickleList (Pickle Li)
mypicklelist-pickle-li.bio: Blog reviews from the MyPickleList site, written as first impressions after a few sessions. They focus on feel, pop, sweet spot size and whether a paddle suits control players or power players, and often note added weight.

nico-the-lefty.name: Nico the Lefty
nico-the-lefty.bio: Publishes paddle reviews on a blog and TikTok, often after many hours of play. Reviews cite lab swing weight, twist weight and spin RPM figures, grit durability, and which player ratings a paddle suits. They describe themselves as a power player.

nikki-maldonado.name: Nikki Maldonado
nikki-maldonado.bio: A YouTube channel with pickleball gear reviews from an intermediate player's view, and co-host of the 99% Pickleball Podcast. Reviews run shot by shot, with 20 repeats per shot, then check swing weight and twist weight afterward.

not-dead-yet-pickleball.name: Not Dead Yet Pickleball
not-dead-yet-pickleball.bio: A YouTube channel that reviews paddles with a focus on recreational and senior players. Videos are mostly head-to-head comparisons, often against Honolulu paddles, and discuss power tier, grit and who a paddle suits.

paddle-addicts.name: Paddle Addicts
paddle-addicts.bio: A YouTube channel focused on paddle reviews that report measured swing weight and twist weight, tuning tape setups and hours of play. Reviews often compare shapes of the same paddle and rate power tier, pop, spin and sweet spot.

paddle-review-hub.name: Paddle Review Hub
paddle-review-hub.bio: A YouTube channel and website describing independent paddle reviews built on court testing, scores and community input. Reviews list weight, swing weight, twist weight and spin RPM, and some cite independent lab spin loss.

paddlecompare.name: PaddleCompare
paddlecompare.bio: A paddle review blog that reports estimated game counts and compares paddles within the same line, such as elongated against widebody shapes. Reviews weigh power, resets, hand speed and forgiveness, and name who each paddle suits.

paddlecompare-johnny-pickleball.name: PaddleCompare (Johnny Pickleball)
paddlecompare-johnny-pickleball.bio: Blog reviews on PaddleCompare based on league, open and recreational play. They rate power, spin, control, resets and hand speed, sometimes out of ten, mostly test paddles stock, and note when a paddle suits defensive or control-first players.

pbvinny.name: PBVinny
pbvinny.bio: A TikTok creator who posts paddle reviews, often after long use and break-in. Reviews frequently compare paddles to the Honolulu J2CR and 11SIX24 Ultre and comment on feel, grit wear, shape and handle length.

pickle-li.name: Pickle Li
pickle-li.bio: A 5.0 pickleball player who posts tips, gameplay, fitness experiments and paddle reviews. Reviews are first impressions after a few days, usually stock, covering pop, power tier, sweet spot and grit, with a score out of ten.

pickle-pick.name: Pickle Pick
pickle-pick.bio: A YouTube channel that reviews paddles with a focus on power, control, feel and on-court performance, through shorts, first impressions and longer reviews. Several reviews follow grit wear and break-in over weeks of use.

pickle-techie.name: Pickle Techie
pickle-techie.bio: A YouTube and TikTok channel covering pickleball technology and performance, from paddle engineering to technique. Reviews include top paddle rankings, head-to-head comparisons and notes on foam cores, core crush and paddle weights.

pickleball-advocate.name: Pickleball Advocate
pickleball-advocate.bio: A YouTube channel that runs free paddle and gear giveaways and reviews new releases. Reviews compare surfaces and grit against current paddles, and often cover Selkirk, Luzz and RPM models and how their feel and pop differ.

pickleball-blast.name: Pickleball Blast
pickleball-blast.bio: A YouTube channel and blog giving opinions on paddles and related gear. Reviews report static weight, swing weight and twist weight, place paddles in a power tier, and cover Six Zero and 11SIX24 lines.

pickleball-effect.name: Pickleball Effect
pickleball-effect.bio: Runs a channel and site with paddle reviews built on measured data: spin in RPM, swing weight, twist weight, speed gun readings and grit wear tests. Reviews lean toward elongated power paddles and often report how much grit texture is retained.

pickleball-effect-braydon-unsicker.name: Pickleball Effect (Braydon Unsicker)
pickleball-effect-braydon-unsicker.bio: Blog reviews from Pickleball Effect that pair on-court play with in-house measurements of static weight, swing weight, twist weight, serve speed and spin. Covers mostly Ronbus paddles and often compares them to earlier versions.

pickleball-medicine.name: Pickleball Medicine 💊
pickleball-medicine.bio: Channel for paddle, equipment and gear reviews, plus a podcast. Reviews focus on Honolulu, Volair and other Gen 4 foam paddles, often side by side, covering feel, sweet spot, twist weight and how shapes compare.

pickleball-on-call.name: Pickleball On Call
pickleball-on-call.bio: Channel describing its paddle reviews as concise and data-driven. Reviews use measurements, radar gun readings and slow motion footage, and several track spin loss after about 10 hours of play. Control is often rated low.

pickleball-paddle-reviews.name: Pickleball Paddle Reviews
pickleball-paddle-reviews.bio: TikTok account posting paddle comparisons, often judging a paddle from both a control player and a power player angle. Frequently mentions RPM, Selkirk, Honolulu and Six Zero models.

pickleball-playbook.name: Pickleball Playbook
pickleball-playbook.bio: Channel for pickleball gear reviews and discounts. Reviews follow a repeated format of power and spin, control, pop and hand speed segments, then skinny singles games, often with two players trading paddles.

pickleball-playbook-austin-hardy.name: Pickleball Playbook - Austin Hardy
pickleball-playbook-austin-hardy.bio: Channel with videos to help players level up their game. Paddle reviews use set drills, hands battles and skinny singles, and often say which skill level suits each paddle, usually intermediate to advanced.

pickleball-playbook-paddles.name: Pickleball Playbook Paddles
pickleball-playbook-paddles.bio: Channel for pickleball gear reviews and discounts. Reviews are mostly live on-court games covering control, power, pop and spin, sometimes with scores out of 10, and often compare a new paddle to one already played.

pickleball-portal.name: Pickleball Portal
pickleball-portal.bio: Blog with hands-on paddle write-ups after a week or more of play. Reviews report serve speed, spin, sweet spot and noise, and often say which type of player a paddle suits.

pickleball-pursuit.name: Pickleball Pursuit
pickleball-pursuit.bio: Channel providing in depth paddle reviews. Reviews focus on feel, power tier, swing weight and twist weight, and sometimes track how grit wears over dozens of games. Often compares paddles within the same brand line.

pickleball-rx.name: Pickleball Rx
pickleball-rx.bio: Channel run by three medical professionals from Mobile, Alabama, aimed at beginner to intermediate players. Reviews are often two-person discussions that compare paddles head to head on power, pop, spin and sweet spot.

pickleball-studio.name: Pickleball Studio
pickleball-studio.bio: Blog and channel with data-heavy paddle reviews. Reviews measure spin with a radar gun and grit roughness with a gauge, often over dozens of games up to about 100, and flag when grit wears faster than claimed.

pickleball-studio-clips.name: Pickleball Studio Clips
pickleball-studio-clips.bio: Channel for short clips from the Pickleball Studio Podcast. Paddle takes come from two reviewers talking through early impressions, often covering swing weight, spin readings, sweet spot and who a paddle suits.

pickleball-tech-dude.name: Pickleball Tech Dude
pickleball-tech-dude.bio: Channel whose description reads Harvard engineer, ex-PPA and pickleball product tester. Reviews cite wear tests such as 10,000 shots, spin retention and quality control across many units.

pickleball-union.name: Pickleball Union
pickleball-union.bio: Blog reviewing paddles after weeks of recreational play. Reviews describe pop, spin, sweet spot and control, and often name the type of player a paddle suits, from beginners to strong intermediates.

pickleball-willy.name: Pickleball Willy
pickleball-willy.bio: YouTube channel with paddle reviews, mostly foam paddles from Luzz, RPM, Selkirk and MARK. Reviews usually state hours played, swing weight and break-in time, and cover how each paddle handles drops, resets and dinks.

pickleballer.name: PickleBaller
pickleballer.bio: YouTube channel and site making paddle videos meant to help players improve. Reviews usually rank a paddle against others on spin, power and control, often covering Honolulu, Luzz, Selkirk and Joola models.

pickleballwilly.name: pickleballwilly
pickleballwilly.bio: TikTok creator posting short paddle takes, often first impressions after a game or a week of play. Reviews cover RPM Jade, Luzz Cannon and Chorus Coda, with attention to spin, pop and grit durability.

pickleheads.name: Pickleheads
pickleheads.bio: Pickleball site with a blog and YouTube channel publishing on-court paddle reviews. Reviews often rate power, control, spin and forgiveness, and cover grit durability, break-in and lead tape setups.

pickletip.name: PickleTip
pickletip.bio: Blog publishing long paddle tests, often 12 to 44 hours and sometimes shared between two testers. Reviews compare paddle shapes side by side and cover break-in, grit wear, swing weight and weighted setups.

rackets-runners-pickleball.name: Rackets & Runners - Pickleball
rackets-runners-pickleball.bio: YouTube channel from Rackets & Runners, a Vancouver business operating since 1978. Reviews are hands-on, with swing weight and twist weight numbers, lead tape setups and notes on sweet spot size.

rallyhaus-pickleball.name: RALLYHAUS PICKLEBALL
rallyhaus-pickleball.bio: YouTube paddle research channel that focuses on real sound and gameplay. Reviews judge paddles in live games, often after a dink board warm up, and report measured weights, break-in and feel.

rye3d-printing.name: RYE3D Printing
rye3d-printing.bio: YouTube channel from a maker of ball hoppers that also posts paddle reviews. The paddle reviews here are all 11SIX24 models, with notes on added weight and whether each suits doubles, singles or beginners.

salt-n-pepper-pickleball.name: Salt N Pepper Pickleball
salt-n-pepper-pickleball.bio: YouTube channel from a passionate player mixing pickleball with personality. Reviews usually describe adding tungsten or tuning tape to reach a target weight, then report spin, feel, kitchen play and arm comfort.

scooter-reviews-stuff.name: Scooter Reviews Stuff
scooter-reviews-stuff.bio: YouTube channel reviewing paddle lines across their shapes, such as Bread & Butter, CRBN and Pickleball Apes. Reviews quote average swing weight and twist weight and often describe tungsten tape tweaks.

smash-pickleball.name: Smash Pickleball
smash-pickleball.bio: YouTube channel with paddle reviews from a player with a tennis background who prefers elongated shapes. Reviews report measured swing weight, weight tape tweaks, and how weight affects hand battles and arm fatigue.

spinwave-pickleball.name: Spinwave Pickleball
spinwave-pickleball.bio: Blog with data-minded paddle reviews, using radar gun serve tests and measured swing weight, twist weight and static weight. Reviews place power, pop and spin on category scales and often compare against the RPM Q2.

sts-pickleball.name: STS PICKLEBALL
sts-pickleball.bio: YouTube channel and blog by Steven, who tests paddles and measures performance. Reviews use a radar gun, swing weight machine and ball machine drills, then rank each paddle against averages in a large paddle database.

supasenpai.name: SupaSenpai
supasenpai.bio: YouTube and TikTok channel reviewing a wide range of pickleball brands for everyday players. Reviews grade serves, drives, spin, hand battles and smashes, and often cover durability and build issues.

the-adventurous-boomer.name: The Adventurous Boomer
the-adventurous-boomer.bio: Blog with written paddle playtests covering power, touch, spin and sound. Reviews focus on the Bread & Butter Loco shapes, the Vanwin Alpha Power and Honolulu models, with notes on how each paddle feels at the kitchen.

the-honest-take.name: The Honest Take
the-honest-take.bio: A YouTube channel with the tagline real reviews and honest takes. Reviews are mostly of Six Zero paddles, with some Luzz and CRBN models, and cover drops, resets, spin and weight setups.

the-new-main-pickleball.name: The New Main Pickleball
the-new-main-pickleball.bio: A YouTube channel that logs long stretches of play on each paddle and measures static, swing and twist weight. Reviews often compare against a paddle they already know, such as the Joola Perseus Pro IV, and track grit wear over hours.

the-pickleball-dad.name: The Pickleball Dad
the-pickleball-dad.bio: A self-described 3.5 DUPR dad sharing paddle and gear reviews, beginner-friendly tips and rec court humor. Reviews often add weight at 3 and 9 o'clock and judge how easy drops, dinks and resets are to dial in.

the-pickleball-pirates.name: The Pickleball Pirates
the-pickleball-pirates.bio: A YouTube channel following amateur players on a quest to 5.0. Their paddle reviews cover elongated and hybrid shapes, often with lead tape added, and several compare different shapes of the same paddle.

the-pickleball-reviews.name: The Pickleball Reviews
the-pickleball-reviews.bio: A paddle review blog that plays each model for 10 to 15 hours or more and publishes measured numbers. Reviews report swing weight, twist weight, spin in RPM and pop speed, and watch grit durability over time.

the-sweet-spot-pickleball.name: The Sweet Spot Pickleball
the-sweet-spot-pickleball.bio: A YouTube channel aimed at everyday players rather than pros. Reviews break paddles down by specs, core design and feel, and often sort power and pop into tiers while comparing shapes and similar models.

tickle-my-pickleball.name: Tickle My Pickleball
tickle-my-pickleball.bio: A paddle review channel and blog that shows gameplay while talking through each paddle. Many reviews are head-to-head tests of several paddles, with swing weight and twist weight measured and stock versus weighted setups noted.

to-pickleball-beyond.name: To Pickleball & Beyond
to-pickleball-beyond.bio: A YouTube channel that describes itself as an average family testing gear, with paddle reviews and real play. Many reviews are first impressions straight out of the box, with notes on power, control and break-in.

unforced-errors-pb.name: Unforced Errors PB
unforced-errors-pb.bio: A pickleball podcast channel from two players who take the sport seriously but not themselves. Their paddle reviews are short and cover feel, power, sweet spot and spin, with attention to hollow versus soft feedback.

unforcederrorspb.name: UnforcedErrorsPB
unforcederrorspb.bio: A pickleball podcast channel from two players who take the sport seriously but not themselves. Reviews are longer on-court write-ups that list swing and twist weight, break-in time and how drops and dinks come together.

vonegypt-pickleball.name: vonEgypt Pickleball
vonegypt-pickleball.bio: A Hudson Valley, NY pickleball channel run by Nick vonEgypt. Reviews often come from recorded matches and tournament play against strong players, with spec rundowns and notes on adding weight.

west-side-pickleball.name: West Side Pickleball
west-side-pickleball.bio: A pickleball channel from a self-described simple guy in West Texas, posting gameplay and weekly reviews. Reviews lean on singles play and side-by-side comparisons with paddles like the Bread & Butter Loco 2 and Boomstik ST.

whiskydink.name: WhiskyDink
whiskydink.bio: A channel where DocMartin combines pickleball with whisky. Paddle reviews often use X-ray and CT imaging, measured specs and sound tests, with driveway sessions comparing several paddles back to back.

womack-pickleball.name: Womack Pickleball
womack-pickleball.bio: A channel that reviews pickleball gear, often using units sent by brands. Reviews list static, swing and twist weight, then place each paddle in the power or all-court category against named paddles like the Boomstik and Q2.

wongsquared.name: Wongsquared
wongsquared.bio: A channel run by Nate, who also enjoys photography and keyboards. Paddle reviews come from a recreational player using bought or borrowed paddles, often comparing Honolulu models and the Luzz Inferno 2.
